paper_metadata.title: Analysis of a hybrid quantum network for classification tasks

experiments.description: Hybrid quantum-classical classifier on a balanced credit-scoring dataset, comparing a single-pass quantum encoding versus data re-uploading, with a classical neural-network baseline.

algorithm.variant: Hybrid classical-quantum neural network (QNet) with and without data re-uploading
algorithm.ansatz: Per-qubit Ry-Rz-Ry rotations followed by CNOT entanglement; variational block repeated across layers
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Not explicitly stated; results reported after training

problem_formulation.encoding_details: A classical neural network maps input features to rotation angles phi_ij, which are then used in Ry(phi_i1) Rz(phi_i2) Ry(phi_i3) on each qubit; qubits are entangled with CNOT gates
problem_formulation.objective_function: Minimize categorical crossentropy for binary classification

problem_instance.description: Credit-scoring binary classification on a balanced sample of a finance dataset

dataset_specification.description: Six features scaled to [0,1]; balanced sample with default rate lifted to 50%; 340 training observations; separate test set used, size not reported

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Features scaled to [0,1]; class balance adjusted to 50% default rate for sample I
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Training and test evaluation using ACC and AUC

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Classical neural network used to downscale features into quantum rotation angles; features scaled to [0,1]
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Softmax output layer; categorical crossentropy loss
implementation_details.training_details: ADAM optimizer in TensorFlow; learning rate 0.01

speedup_claims.conditions: Balanced credit-scoring sample with nqubits = nlayers = 8
speedup_claims.caveats: No runtime or asymptotic speedup is reported; only predictive performance improvements are discussed.

experiments.description: Hybrid quantum-classical classifier on an unbalanced credit-scoring dataset, comparing single-pass quantum encoding versus data re-uploading, with a classical neural-network baseline.

algorithm.variant: Hybrid classical-quantum neural network (QNet) with and without data re-uploading
algorithm.ansatz: Per-qubit Ry-Rz-Ry rotations followed by CNOT entanglement; variational block repeated across layers
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Not explicitly stated; results reported after training

problem_formulation.encoding_details: A classical neural network maps input features to rotation angles phi_ij, which are then used in Ry(phi_i1) Rz(phi_i2) Ry(phi_i3) on each qubit; qubits are entangled with CNOT gates
problem_formulation.objective_function: Minimize categorical crossentropy for binary classification

problem_instance.description: Credit-scoring binary classification on the original unbalanced finance dataset

dataset_specification.description: Six features scaled to [0,1]; original unbalanced class distribution with default rate about 16.67%; 900 training cases; separate test set used, size not reported

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Features scaled to [0,1]; original unbalanced class distribution retained
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Training and test evaluation using ACC and AUC

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Classical neural network used to downscale features into quantum rotation angles; features scaled to [0,1]
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Softmax output layer; categorical crossentropy loss
implementation_details.training_details: ADAM optimizer in TensorFlow; learning rate 0.01

speedup_claims.conditions: Unbalanced credit-scoring sample with nqubits = nlayers = 8
speedup_claims.caveats: No runtime or asymptotic speedup is reported; the paper emphasizes that accuracy alone is misleading for the unbalanced dataset and AUC differs across models.

experiments.description: Hybrid quantum-classical classifier on MNIST handwritten digits, evaluated against a classical neural-network baseline and studied across different qubit and layer counts.

algorithm.variant: Hybrid classical-quantum neural network (QNet) with data re-uploading
algorithm.ansatz: Per-qubit Ry-Rz-Ry rotations followed by CNOT entanglement; variational block repeated across layers
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Not explicitly stated; training evaluated over epochs

problem_formulation.encoding_details: A classical neural network maps image features to rotation angles phi_ij, which are then used in Ry(phi_i1) Rz(phi_i2) Ry(phi_i3) on each qubit; qubits are entangled with CNOT gates

dataset_specification.description: 28x28 grayscale images; 60,000 training images and 10,000 test images exist in the full dataset, but this experiment uses 1,000 training images and the full 10,000-image test set

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Images treated as 784 features; classical network used to downscale to quantum parameters
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Training and test ACC; confusion matrix on training data; performance compared to classical network; scalability examined over nqubits in [2,4,8,12] and varying nlayers

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Classical neural network used to downscale 784 image features into quantum rotation angles
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Softmax output layer; categorical crossentropy loss
implementation_details.training_details: ADAM optimizer in TensorFlow; learning rate 0.01; 30 epochs mentioned in regularization experiments

speedup_claims.conditions: MNIST with 1,000 training images and 10,000 test images; nqubits = nlayers = 8 in the main comparison
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper claims faster learning progress for the hybrid model, but no wall-clock training time is reported.

experiments.description: Regularization study for the MNIST hybrid classifier using dropout between the quantum and classical output networks.

algorithm.variant: Hybrid classical-quantum neural network with dropout regularization
algorithm.ansatz: Per-qubit Ry-Rz-Ry rotations followed by CNOT entanglement; variational block repeated across layers
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Not explicitly stated; reported after 30 epochs

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Same MNIST-to-quantum-parameter mapping as the main hybrid model; dropout applied to measurement values before the second classical network
problem_formulation.objective_function: Minimize categorical crossentropy with dropout regularization
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Dropout layer sets measurement values randomly to zero with probability 0.58

problem_instance.description: MNIST handwritten digit classification with regularization

dataset_specification.description: Same MNIST setup as the main experiment; 1,000 training images and 10,000 test images

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Classical network used to downscale 784 image features into quantum parameters
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Training ACC compared to test ACC after dropout regularization

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Classical neural network used to downscale 784 image features into quantum rotation angles
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Dropout between quantum and classical layers; softmax output layer; categorical crossentropy loss
implementation_details.training_details: ADAM optimizer in TensorFlow; learning rate 0.01; 30 epochs

speedup_claims.conditions: MNIST regularization experiment with dropout probability 0.58, nqubits = nlayers = 8, after 30 epochs
speedup_claims.caveats: This is a regularization result, not a computational speedup claim.

experiments.description: Regularization study for the MNIST hybrid classifier using L2 penalties on either the quantum input angles or the measured qubit outputs.

algorithm.variant: Hybrid classical-quantum neural network with L2 regularization
algorithm.ansatz: Per-qubit Ry-Rz-Ry rotations followed by CNOT entanglement; variational block repeated across layers
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Not explicitly stated; regularization effect assessed during training

regularized_terms: angles fed into the quantum network

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Same MNIST-to-quantum-parameter mapping as the main hybrid model; L2 regularization applied either to the input angles or to the measurement outputs
problem_formulation.objective_function: Minimize categorical crossentropy plus L2 regularization terms
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: L2 penalty terms added to the loss function

problem_instance.description: MNIST handwritten digit classification with L2 regularization

dataset_specification.description: Same MNIST setup as the main experiment; 1,000 training images and 10,000 test images

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Classical network used to downscale 784 image features into quantum parameters
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Training and validation ACC compared under different L2 regularization placements

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Classical neural network used to downscale 784 image features into quantum rotation angles
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Softmax output layer; categorical crossentropy loss; L2 regularization added to loss
implementation_details.training_details: ADAM optimizer in TensorFlow; learning rate 0.01

speedup_claims.conditions: MNIST regularization experiment with L2 penalties on angles or measurement values
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper reports qualitative conclusions: regularizing measurement values reduces overfitting, while regularizing input angles destroys classification ability. No exact accuracy values are given.
